Dispute Guidance (Consultation)

Structured preparation and case-building before you lodge a rent complaint or respond to one. File review, evidence audit, and strategic options.

Why You Need This Service

You've hit a conflict with your tenant. Maybe they won't pay the agreed rent. Maybe you want to evict. Maybe they're claiming the rent is too high. Whatever the issue, you're thinking about going to the Rent Control Department.

Before you file anything, you need to know:

  • Do you actually have a strong case?
  • What evidence will matter to the magistrate?
  • What are your legal options?
  • What paperwork do you need before filing?
  • What could go wrong and how do you mitigate it?

This consultation is your case review before you walk into Rent Court. It's the difference between filing with a strong position and filing and losing.

What We Do

  • File Review: You bring your documents and tell us the situation
  • Evidence Audit: What you have, what's strong, what's weak
  • Chronology Building: Timeline of events that matter to your case
  • Legal Options: What you can and cannot do under Act 220
  • Magistrate Perspective: What a Rent Magistrate will want to see
  • Risk Assessment: What could go against you and how to prepare

What You Get

  • Case Assessment: Written summary of strengths and weaknesses
  • Evidence Checklist: What documents to bring to Rent Court
  • Strategic Advice: How to present your case
  • Next Steps: What to do immediately before filing
  • Fallback Options: What to do if you lose and what to appeal on

When You Need This Service

  • A tenant has refused to pay and you're considering eviction
  • You want to increase rent and the tenant is fighting it
  • A tenant has lodged a complaint against you and you need to respond
  • You're not sure if you can legally evict or what steps are required
  • You're about to file a complaint but want professional review first

The Real Value

A GHS 200 consultation now can save you thousands in a lost case or months of drawn-out dispute. Most landlords go to Rent Court with weak files and lose. This service prevents that.
